verses.text: The men of Ephraim said to Gideon, "Why have you treated us like this? Why did you not call us when you went to fight Midian?" And they argued with him angrily.
But he answered them, "What have I done compared to you? Are not the leftover grapes of Ephraim better than the whole grape harvest of my clan, Abiezer?
God gave Oreb and Zeeb, the Midianite leaders, into your hands. What could I do compared to you?" When he said this, they stopped being angry with him.
Gideon and his three hundred men came to the Jordan and crossed it. They were exhausted, but they kept chasing the enemy.
He said to the men of Sukkoth, "Please give my soldiers some bread. They are worn out, and I am still chasing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian."
But the officials of Sukkoth said, "Have you already captured Zebah and Zalmunna? Why should we give bread to your army?"
Gideon replied, "Just for that, when the LORD has given Zebah and Zalmunna into my hands, I will tear your flesh with desert thorns and briers."
From there he went up to Penuel and asked the same of them, but they answered him as the men of Sukkoth had.
So he said to the men of Penuel, "When I come back safely, I will tear down this tower."

Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor with an army of about fifteen thousand men. These were all that were left of the armies of the eastern peoples, because a hundred and twenty thousand swordsmen had been killed.
Gideon went up along the road of the tent dwellers east of Nobah and Jogbehah and attacked the army by surprise, while they felt safe.
Zebah and Zalmunna, the two kings of Midian, ran away, but he chased them and captured them, and he threw their whole army into panic.
Then Gideon son of Joash came back from the battle by the Pass of Heres.
He caught a young man from Sukkoth and questioned him. The young man wrote down for him the names of the seventy-seven officials and elders of Sukkoth.

Then Gideon came to the men of Sukkoth and said, "Here are Zebah and Zalmunna. You made fun of me about them, saying, 'Have you already captured Zebah and Zalmunna? Why should we give bread to your worn-out men?'"
He took the elders of the town and taught the men of Sukkoth a lesson by punishing them with desert thorns and briers.
He also tore down the tower of Penuel and killed the men of the town.
Then he asked Zebah and Zalmunna, "What were the men you killed at Tabor like?" They answered, "They were like you. Each one looked like a king's son."
Gideon said, "They were my brothers, the sons of my own mother. As surely as the LORD lives, if you had spared their lives, I would not kill you."
He turned to Jether, his oldest son, and said, "Kill them!" But Jether did not draw his sword, because he was only a boy and was afraid.
Zebah and Zalmunna said, "Come, do it yourself. A man is judged by his strength." So Gideon stepped forward and killed them, and took the moon-shaped ornaments off their camels' necks.
The Israelites said to Gideon, "Rule over us, you, your son and your grandson, because you have saved us from Midian."
But Gideon told them, "I will not rule over you, and my son will not rule over you. The LORD will rule over you."
But he said, "I do have one request. Each of you give me an earring from the things you took in battle." It was the custom of the Ishmaelites to wear gold earrings.
They answered, "We will gladly give them." So they spread out a cloak, and each man threw an earring onto it from what he had taken.
The gold earrings he asked for weighed about twenty kilograms. This did not count the ornaments, the necklaces, the purple clothes worn by the kings of Midian, or the chains on their camels' necks.
Gideon made the gold into an ephod, a priestly vest, and put it in his town, Ophrah. All Israel was unfaithful to God by worshipping it there, and it became a trap for Gideon and his family.
So Midian was defeated by the Israelites and did not rise up again. In Gideon's lifetime the land had peace for forty years.
Jerub-Baal son of Joash went back home to live.
Gideon had seventy sons of his own, because he had many wives.
His concubine, who lived in Shechem, also gave birth to a son, whom he named Abimelek.
Gideon son of Joash died at a good old age and was buried in the tomb of his father Joash in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
As soon as Gideon died, the Israelites were again unfaithful to God and worshipped the Baals. They made Baal-Berith their god.
They forgot the LORD their God, who had saved them from all their enemies around them.
They also were not loyal to the family of Jerub-Baal, that is Gideon, for all the good things he had done for Israel.
